Hi Patricia / Kevin —

Thanks for the RFP and the worksheet — we reviewed the questions and can deliver both items you requested. Quick plan:

- One-page narrative summarizing Redwood's de-id policy, technical controls, and risk model (suitable for your legal/security teams).
- Technical appendix with examples: deterministic masking, k-anonymity thresholds we apply for export artifacts, and our tokenization/PHI redaction pipeline.
- Implementation schedule: draft BAA within 5 business days, evidence handoff (SOC/SIG) packaged in week 2, pilot deployment in week 4, full production by week 7 — we can compress aggressive workstreams if procurement confirms a 6-week close.

Laura will assemble the detailed playbook and Gantt; copying her to coordinate artifacts. Can you confirm: do you require NIST 800-53 mappings in the appendix or is the HITRUST mapping sufficient? Also indicate whether the pilot must be within your VPC or if Lakemont is ok with a dedicated isolated tenancy in our Hosted environment.

I will attach the de-id playbook and an implementation schedule in the next internal email.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

Date: 2027-07-12T14:00:00-04:00
Subject: ACTION: Lakemont RFP deliverables + owners (see timeline)

Team —

Patricia at Lakemont sent the RFP (attached). We need a concise deliverable set by EOD Friday (2 business days):

- Laura: One-page narrative + de-id playbook (technical appendix). Use the template in Drive (linked). Include: 1) ingestion-time redaction rules, 2) stored KV cache policies, 3) export/analytics anonymization approach (example queries).
- Priyom: Implementation schedule Gantt (week-by-week, dependencies), and a list of evidence artifacts we can hand off (SOC2, SIG-Lite, encryption key rotation logs). Note expected packaging for procurement.

Attachments to include with the response: redwood_deid_playbook_v1.pdf, implementation_schedule_gantt.xlsx. I'll review drafts and handle legal/procurement alignment.

Thanks — please mark comments in the Drive doc so I can iterate quickly.

Sergio

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-13T10:32:00-04:00
Subject: DRAFT: Lakemont de-id playbook + schedule (attached)

Sergio / Priyom —

Attached are the two artifacts: redwood_deid_playbook_v1.pdf and implementation_schedule_gantt.xlsx. Highlights below (one-page narrative excerpt):

- De-identification approach: We perform tiered de-identification at ingestion, model-serving, and export boundaries. Ingestion-time scrubbing applies deterministic redaction rules (PHI patterns), PII detectors, and optional tokenization. For analytics exports we apply k-anonymity and differential privacy noise where required.
- Technical controls: KV cache TTLs, encryption-at-rest (AES-256), envelope encryption with customer or Redwood KMS, and field-level access controls.
- Evidence we will hand off: SOC 2 Type II report, SIG-Lite response, sample key rotation audit logs, and a sanitized logs package for Lakemont review.
- BAA / onboarding: We propose a two-step BAA sign & evidence handoff: 1) Legal execution of BAA + interim scoping addendum (5 business days), 2) Evidence package and technical onboarding (days 6–15), 3) Pilot validation and ops runbook handover (days 16–30).

Notes / Exceptions:
- Runtime cache retention: standard 30-day TTL; to support Lakemont's shorter retention ask, we recommend a proxy that truncates caches per-route — engineering estimate: 3–4 weeks to implement.
- NIST 800-53 mapping: we included a HITRUST-to-NIST crosswalk appendix; we can produce a full NIST mapping on request (additional 4 business days).

Quoted earlier request for context:
> "Can you summarize Redwood's de-identification strategy for ingestion pipelines and model training-eligible logs?"

Next steps: Sergio to review and send to Patricia with attachments; Priyom to verify the evidence bundle naming conventions.

Laura Bennett
Principal Security PM, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_deid_playbook_v1.pdf, implementation_schedule_gantt.xlsx

2) On evidence packaging: can you confirm the format for the sanitized logs package (CSV vs gzipped JSON) and whether the package will include example audit queries?

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

Date: 2027-07-14T16:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Lakemont RFP: de-identification approach and BAA transition plan

Hi Patricia —

Quick answers:

1) BAA timeline assumptions: 5 business days assumes standard review with minor technical clarifications only (no legal redlines). If Lakemont returns a set of substantive redlines, we will engage legal and expect a 7–12 business day turn depending on complexity; we can accelerate with a focused 1:1 negotiation session (same-day block) but that requires sign-off to prioritize. We'll call that an expedited route if procurement wants to trade budget/discount for faster turnaround.

2) Sanitized logs package: default format is gzipped JSON (structured events) plus a CSV summary index for quick inspection. We include sample audit queries (SQL and Elasticsearch DSL) in a readme inside the package. If you require CSV-only, we can produce that but it increases the file size and may require additional field flattening.

Next steps: If procurement/legal confirms they will not submit heavy redlines we will: 1) upload the draft BAA to DocuSign by EOD tomorrow (link to be shared), 2) deliver the sanitized logs package as a secure Drive link during week 2, and 3) begin pilot provisioning week 4.

Happy to join a call with your legal team; please propose times.

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
